newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais expects big 1997 profit-paper.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais expects big 1997 profit-paper.

text.p: State-owned bank Credit Lyonnais expects to report between 3.4 and 3.7 billion francs of net attributable profit for 1997 after a profit close to 300 million francs for 1996, the newspaper Les Echos said on Thursday.
The bank declined comment on the report.
"The recovery of Credit Lyonnais' proper activities is taking place faster and more solidly than expected," it said.

"Within the next few weeks, chairman Jean Peyrelevade is expected to report a net attributable profit of close to 300 million francs for 1996...The forecasts for 1997 signal a spectacular rebound -- it should generate this year between 3.4 and 3.7 billion francs of net attributable profit, that is to say, levels comparable to the performances of Banque Nationale de Paris or Societe Generale," it said.
It said the figures were presented at a December board meeting.
The bright prospects are due to a strong contribution from market activities, good results at the U.S. and Asian businesses, and a rebound in the retail banking network in France, the newspaper said.

It said Finance Minister Arthuis was expected to present the government's latest assistance plan for the bank to the European Commission on Thursday or Friday, but added that the final figures had not yet been set.
